subject: FinTrust SIG intake — SDLC controls snapshot & evidence handoff
messages:
From: Amanda Li <amanda.li@fintrust.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: security@fintrust.com
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG intake — SDLC artifacts we need

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. FinTrust's questionnaire intake team is starting the SIG review and we need a compact set of artifacts demonstrating your Secure SDLC controls for the areas below: code review practices (sample PRs + reviewer roles), CI/CD controls (pipeline enforcement, signed artifacts, transient credentials), secrets management (vaulting/KMS & rotation policy), and change management (approval gates, emergency patch process).

To keep the assessor's intake light, could you provide:
- A manifest listing each artifact and where to download it (single spreadsheet preferred)
- 2 redacted PRs that show code review enforcement and required approvers
- A short snippet or diagram of your CI pipeline and where checks/gates run (e.g. lint, SAST, signed build step)
- Evidence of ephemeral credential usage for runners and any PR/merge guardrail config
- Your change management policy (how emergency changes are recorded and approved)

If you have a single archive or a Drive folder we can point the assessor to, that'd be ideal. Tom (cc) is the external assessor who will formalize the SIG intake. We're aiming to start intake review next Wednesday (04/02).

Appreciate a delivery plan and any constraints (redactions, timelines).

Best,
Amanda
Security Intake Lead
FinTrust

--
Attachments: none
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Amanda Li <amanda.li@fintrust.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG intake — SDLC artifacts we need

Amanda — thanks for the checklist and timeline.

We can do that. High-level plan (deliver by EOD Mon 03/29, final Drive bundle by Tue 03/30):
1) Deliver a manifest (spreadsheet) that maps each ask to a document or Drive link.
2) Attach two redacted PRs and a short sampling report that explains redaction and selection criteria.
3) Include a CI pipeline snippet (we'll export the pipeline steps relevant to gates) and an annotated diagram that shows where SAST/lint/signing occurs.
4) Provide a secrets management summary + rotation cadence and a sanitized KMS audit excerpt.
5) Supply our change management runbook (including emergency patch steps) and a short table of recent emergency patches with approver entries.

Irene, can you assemble the manifest and the redacted PRs? Jordan, please export the pipeline YAML and write a one-page annotation for the assessor. Lauren, I'll loop you for the runbook export and any legal redaction notes.

Amanda — I'll attach the manifest and the initial artifacts for your review by EOD Monday. If the assessor needs access to a read-only Drive, we can share it and provide a time-boxed link; let us know which you prefer.

Regards,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

--

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG intake — SDLC artifacts we need

Sean — I'm putting the pieces together. Quick notes for the intake artifacts:

- PR sampling: I selected two representative, redacted PRs from our main repo (service-proxy). Both include required approver hooks enforced by branch protection and CODEOWNERS. Redactions: customer data and any proprietary SQL snippets removed. See code-review-sampling-report-2027-03.pdf (attached) for selection rationale and reviewer mapping.

- CI/CD: Jordan exported the pipeline YAML; main enforcement points are:
  * pre-merge SAST job (fails build on high severity)
  * signed artifact step (we sign builds using our internal signing key stored in KMS)
  * ephemeral runner token issuance (short TTL tokens issued via ephemeral K8s service account flow)

  Attached: ci_pipeline_config_snippet.yaml (redacted), and an internal note showing how the signed artifact step is invoked.

- Secrets management: We use a central vault (HashiCorp Vault) backed by a cloud KMS for key encryption. Rotation policy: root wrapping keys rotated quarterly; application-level secrets rotated per-service on a 90-day cadence or on demand. We'll include an excerpt from the Vault audit (sanitized).

- Change management: Our runbook includes: change request ticket in Jira, automated PR link in the ticket, approval matrix (who can approve normal vs emergency), and post-deploy signoff. Emergency patch path requires 2 technical approvers + one manager after deployment. We will export the runbook PDF and a short CSV of recent emergency patch entries with approver names.

I'm attaching the manifest and the two redacted PR links (redacted URLs) in the Drive bundle.

Irene Choi
Director, Engineering Security
Redwood Inference

--

Sean / Irene —

Thanks — this looks good and full enough to start intake. A few follow-ups from Tom (assessor):

- Can you include the branch protection rule screenshot (showing required status checks + required approvers)? If you need to blur team names, that's fine.
- For signed artifacts: a short statement of the key custody policy (who has access to the signing key) is sufficient. We don't need private keys — just custody and signing invocation evidence.
- For Vault audit: a 7-day window of the audit showing creation/rotation events would be ideal (redacted).

If you can get the Drive share to Tom with read-only access by EOD Tue 03/30, we can start the assessor walkthrough on Wed. We'll accept the manifest as the top-level index.

Amanda
